SMTO-GML-0060 — Too many emails match this request

GUID: 85749841-3619-4e3b-b569-b4853e4c5e47
Slug: gmail-selection-limit-exceeded
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-client-actions

What happened

  • More emails matched than one request can handle (at most 50,000, or a lower limit if one was set). SMTO stopped before changing any email for this request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again with a narrower request, for example only emails from one sender, with one label, or older than a certain date. A smaller set fits within the limit, so SMTO can check the full list before changing anything.
  2. If a lower limit was set for this request, ask SMTO to raise it, up to 50,000 emails. The request stops as soon as the matches pass whatever limit was set.
  3. For very large clean-ups, split the work into several requests, such as one per year. Each request can handle at most 50,000 emails, however it is worded.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports how many emails it selected, within the limit, and the action goes ahead.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat a result that covers only part of the matching emails as if it covered all of them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail selection stopped before any write because query pagination or thread expansion exceeded max_messages (hard maximum 50,000).

What this means

  • The workflow stops before its first write when pagination or thread expansion exceeds max_messages, whose hard maximum is 50000.

Why this can happen

  • The workflow stops before its first write when pagination or thread expansion exceeds max_messages, whose hard maximum is 50000.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected account, action arguments and operation reference; do not infer mailbox effects from the error alone.

How to fix it

  • Narrow the Gmail query, scope, message_ids or thread_ids, or raise a lower max_messages up to 50,000 (GmailSelection.max_messages). agent_runtime/skills/gmail/workflows.select fails before any mutation; split larger jobs into several bounded selections.
  • Choose an explicit narrower scope or query, or raise a lower max_messages value up to 50000.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose an explicit narrower scope or query, or raise a lower max_messages value up to 50000.

How to verify the fix

  • The new selection fits its stated limit before mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not present a truncated subset as all matching mail.

Technical notes

  • This check rejects new work before its write. It does not undo previous confirmed effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
